text:
Alex: Opening thread for an escalated customer issue — Go client streaming gets fragmented/duplicated output when the client refreshes auth and reconnects quickly. Customer says JSON sometimes ends up malformed. Filing under INC-4477.
Maya: Which SDK + client stack are they using? Go standard lib or a helper lib? Any repro? :thinking_face:
Alex: Go SDK v0.9.2 (our official package) and also a small in-house wrapper that reads chunked SSE-like stream via http.Response.Body. They included a minimal repro and raw frame capture.
Customer Dev (copied): "We see final tokens cut off, then a new connection sends overlapping bytes. Sometimes the same tokens appear twice. It started after we moved to short-lived bearer tokens and auto-refresh. It breaks our JSON aggregator and we get double billing for some requests."
Kevin: @Alex can you paste the raw frames? Also confirm whether the server emits an `id:` SSE field. Our Go client relies on `event-id` for dedupe if present.
Alex: Customer sent raw capture (sanitized):
```
: open stream (conn A)
data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello, this is the res"}}]
data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"ponse end"}}]
[data: [DONE] missing here sometimes]
: 401 -> client refresh token
: close conn A
: new stream (conn B)
data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello, this is the res"}}]
data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"ponse end"}}]
data: [DONE]
```
Alex: In some runs, conn A's last bytes ("ponse end") interleave with conn B's opening frame so the aggregator concatenates and gets "response endponse end" or truncated JSON when [DONE] was missing.
Maya: That looks like the server flushed a leftover tail from conn A into the sink after conn B was accepted. Does the Go SDK attempt to resume automatically?
Alex: Our Go SDK has a streaming iterator API `stream.Next(ctx) -> []byte` which yields chunks. The customer is reading `for stream.Next(ctx) { buf.Write(chunk) }` while their token refresh goroutine performs `client.Refresh()` and recreates `stream` quickly.
Jordan: SRE: this matches a race we've seen in the stream-sink merging path: when a reconnect occurs we sometimes flush any buffered bytes to the shared sink without verifying the active connection ID. If conn B races in, the sink doesn't drop the tail from conn A. I'll correlate with auth-change commits.
Kevin: I rolled the auth refresh change last week (runtime PR #4658) that added proactive reconnect on 401. Could have introduced a handoff bug.
Support Bot: Deploy runtime PR #4658 completed 2024-06-11 02:17:00Z :white_check_mark:
Alex: Customer repro steps (condensed):
1) create stream with short-lived token (TTL ~4s)
2) start a long-ish model response (>5s) so tokens expire mid-stream
3) client receives 401, calls Refresh(), then immediately reopens stream
4) occasionally the final bytes from the old stream are emitted to the sink after the new connection started
5) consumer sees duplicated or concatenated fragments -> broken JSON or duplicate content

Maya: Initial mitigation recommendations sent to customer: increase token TTL if possible, or perform refresh proactively before expiry (e.g., refresh at TTL*0.8). Also add short backoff between close/open (100-250ms) and simple dedupe by hashing last N bytes or using an `event-id` header when present.
Customer Dev (reply): They can't change token TTL and their system relies on immediate refresh. They asked for a server-side fix.
Jordan: Priority assessment: corrupt output + double-billing risk -> escalate to P1. We'll need a hotfix that ensures connection-boundary guarantees for buffered frames.
Kevin: Local staging repro: I can reproduce with a test that issues an auth-refresh mid-stream. Observed logs: 
```
[staging] conn-A read 512 bytes -> buffered tail 48 bytes
[staging] conn-B accepted for same client-id
[staging] stream-sink flush tail -> included in conn-B output path
```
Kevin: Root cause: stream-sink doesn't tag buffered frames with the origin connection id, so flushes can cross-session. Fix plan: tag frames by conn-id and only deliver frames to active session; when a reconnect occurs, drop or dead-letter frames tied to previous conn. Also consider adding an `id:` (event-id) SSE field per emitted logical chunk for client-side dedupe.
Maya: Action items:
- Kevin: PR to add conn-id guard + unit/integration tests (ETA 3h)
- Jordan: add runtime metric `sse.cross_conn_tail_flush` alerting when we drop/observe tail flushes (ETA 6h)
- Maya: update support reply with timeline and temporary client-side hardening snippet (ETA 30m)
- Finance-Billing: watch INC-4477 for suspicious double-charge patterns (ETA immediate)

Finance-Billing: acknowledged; we'll suspend automatic settlement for that org until the investigation completes and wave refunds if needed.
Alex: Proposed quick server-side patch: on auth-refresh handshake, perform an atomic swap of active-conn pointer before accepting new frames; ensure any pending buffer from old conn is not mixed. If buffer exists, either drop or deliver to dead-letter queue for post-mortem.
Kevin: I'll prototype that and push a staging PR. Also adding a small compatibility header `x-rw-sse-id: <uuid>` on each chunk so clients can dedupe: clients can ignore repeated IDs. Need to update SDK to expose ids in iterator.
Maya: For the Go SDK we should also make the streaming iterator expose an `ID()` for the last chunk so wrappers can use it to dedupe. Add this to v0.9.3 changelog.
Jordan: Test matrix for patch:
- rapid reconnect on 401 with TTL 1s
- concurrent token refresh + multiple worker streams
- ensure no frame duplication and that old conn buffers are not delivered to new conn

Kevin: Opening PR now to staging with tests and a changelog entry. Will link once created.
Alex: Customer asked for a short-term snippet (Go) for client-side dedupe. I drafted and sent: 
```
// naive dedupe: keep last event hash
var lastHash string
for stream.Next(ctx) {
  h := hash(stream.Chunk())
  if h == lastHash { continue }
  lastHash = h
  process(stream.Chunk())
}
```
Maya: Also suggested small linear backoff before reopening stream to reduce handoff race: sleep 150ms after close before new EventSource.
Customer Dev (reply): Applied dedupe hack and backoff; reduced occurrences but still sees one in 200 requests. Wants confirmation of server fix timeline.
Jordan: Given billing exposure, we should aim to ship to production within 24h for the conn-id guard.
Kevin: Agreed. I'll tag the PR as hotfix-prod and request expedited review.
Support Bot: INC-4477 updated: customer applied temporary mitigations; awaiting patch.
Alex: I'll keep the customer posted and escalate billing as needed. Thanks all. reactions: :thumbsup: :warning:
